svg.title: Bindings and languages
svg.desc: One annotated Rust bridge and Diplomat generate six language surfaces that share naming, byte, and JSON contracts.

g.aria-label: The core is annotated in src/bridge
Diplomat generates the JavaScript / TypeScript surface
Diplomat generates the Kotlin / JVM surface
Native Rust calls the core directly, bypassing Diplomat

g.title: Rust core
g.desc: Schematics, fields, and simulation live here once.

g.title: Annotations
g.desc: Attributes mark what may cross the boundary.

g.title: JavaScript / TypeScript
g.desc: WASM keeps the same byte and JSON contracts in browsers and Node; nothing native to build or ship.

g.title: Python
g.desc: A nanobind native module: Python objects wrap the same byte contract with no copies in between.

g.title: Kotlin / JVM
g.desc: JNA loads the shared library on the JVM and calls the generated symbol names directly.

g.title: PHP
g.desc: PHP FFI binds the C ABI at runtime; names and payload shapes are generated, never hand-written.

g.title: C
g.desc: Stable ABI headers are the contract every other binding is built on; the symbols never drift.

g.title: C++
g.desc: Typed wrappers add RAII and real types over the same exported C symbols, so nothing is duplicated.

g.title: Rust
g.desc: Native Rust skips the bridge entirely: crates depend on the core and call its API directly.

text.tspan: Annotate the core once in src/bridge; Diplomat generates naming, byte and JSON contracts for every surface.
